answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake for a fixed period before it may influence allocation; votes are weighted by stake, and proven double-signing forfeits the lock. Splitting one stake across a gale of aliases creates no extra voting power, while flooding the orchard with identities ties up more capital per unit of influence. The attacker pays an opportunity cost and risks losing the stake, rather than merely minting another relic-like account.
